archetype.name: Retooling (shootout offense)
archetype.definition: A first-year staff has rebuilt the passing game around a veteran quarterback faster than anyone expected, but the defense still bleeds points and the run game doesn't work, so the result is a .500 team rather than a contender.

report.headline: Cousins rebuilt the passing game; a leaky defense keeps giving it back.
report.take:
A year ago this was the worst offense in football, last in offensive EPA (-0.192) and last in scoring at 14.2 points a game. Under first-year coach Klint Kubiak, with Kirk Cousins starting every week, the Raiders score 26.1 a game (6th) and pass at 0.201 EPA a dropback (7th). The passing game runs through the tight ends. Brock Bowers leads the team in targets despite playing only six games, and Michael Mayer is close behind. Cousins is almost never sacked: a 0.035 sack rate, 4th. That is a real, structural change, not a hot streak.

The record isn't driven by that offense alone. It is the offense against a defense that can't get off the field. The Raiders allow 28.1 points a game (29th), opponents succeed on 47% of snaps (27th), and they score touchdowns on 78.6% of red-zone trips (29th). Since the calendar turned to October, every opponent has scored at least 30. The 3-0 start came against Miami, the Chargers and the Saints, and the losing stretch that followed came against Kansas City, New England, Buffalo and the Rams. The record matches the play almost exactly: 0.33 wins over expected, and a point differential that implies 3.7 wins.

The defense's surface numbers hide two things. First, the pass rush is elite on paper, 2nd in pressure rate (0.311) and 4th in QB hit rate, yet pass EPA allowed is only 23rd. Offenses beat the rush by getting the ball out short, and against short passes this defense is dead last (0.259 EPA). Second, 12 takeaways (2nd) are propping things up. Without them the scoring defense would look even worse, and takeaway rates rarely hold. On offense, the run game is a hole: 3.12 yards a carry, last in yards before contact and in run success. That points to the line rather than Ashton Jeanty, and it is why rushing EPA was negative in every game.

The Book has been slow to adjust. The Raiders lead the league covering 71.4% of the time, because the market priced last year's team. From here the shape of the season depends on the defense. The offense should keep scoring, but a back half with Denver twice and a trip to Kansas City asks a 22nd-ranked defense to win shootouts against the teams ahead of it in the division.

strengths.title: A genuinely efficient passing game
strengths.body: Cousins has turned the league's worst offense into a top-ten pass unit, leaning on Bowers and Mayer at tight end and avoiding negative plays. The passing EPA has risen through the season, peaking at 16.4 against the Jets. Because it rests on a veteran quarterback and good protection rather than a few long plays, it should largely hold.

strengths.title: Pass rush that wins quickly
strengths.body: The front gets home: 2nd in pressure rate and 4th in QB hit rate, with five sacks in the opener alone. That is a repeatable skill. It gives the defense a floor against quarterbacks who hold the ball, even if it hasn't translated into stopping passes overall.

strengths.title: Winning the turnover battle
strengths.body: Twelve takeaways rank 2nd, and the offense protects the ball well enough for a +5 turnover margin. That has been the difference in the wins, including four takeaways at New Orleans. Some of it comes from the pass rush forcing hurried throws, but takeaway rates this high usually come down, so don't bank on the full margin.

concerns.title: Short passes and red zone defense
concerns.body: The defense ranks last against short passes and 29th in red-zone touchdown rate. Offenses neutralize the pass rush with quick throws, then finish drives. This isn't scheme noise: it has shown up against every competent offense since October. It is the main reason this team is .500 instead of better.

concerns.title: No run game, and it's the line
concerns.body: The Raiders are 31st in yards per carry and last in both yards before contact and run success. With backs met almost immediately, the problem is blocking, not Jeanty. It makes the offense one-dimensional and kills its ability to protect a lead, and nothing in the dossier suggests a fix is coming.

concerns.title: Explosive runs against the defense
concerns.body: The run defense's yardage looks fine, but it gives up explosive runs at the 31st-ranked rate and lead backs beat their averages against it. A 199-yard rushing day for the Rams showed how quickly it can break. Missed tackles (22nd) suggest this is a personnel issue that will persist.

trend.note: A 3-0 start against soft opponents gave way to four straight losses when the defense started allowing 30-plus every week. The passing game kept improving throughout and carried a 38-33 win at the Jets.

nextGame.headline: At the league's best team, a run defense that erases Vegas's
nextGame.body:
San Francisco is 6-1 and first in net EPA, with the league's top run-success offense and the stingiest run defense by EPA. That matchup is brutal for a Raiders team that can't run and can't stop the explosive run. The 49ers' line allows pressure at the 3rd-lowest rate, which blunts the one thing this Raiders defense does well. The Book has the Raiders as 10-point underdogs (+410) with a 51.5 total. The best opening is through the air: the 49ers are 24th against short passes, which is exactly where Cousins and the tight ends live.

The 49ers come off a bye with a lot of help possibly returning. Christian McCaffrey's hamstring strain is described as mild and he's expected to be ready. Mike Evans is expected back, Deebo Samuel and Nick Bosa have a chance to play, and safety Marques Sigle and corner Upton Stout are questionable. For the Raiders, corner Darien Porter left the Jets game with a groin injury and is questionable. He's a rotational 42%-snap player, but the secondary is already thin on answers.

waysToWin.title: Live in the short passing game
waysToWin.body: Concede the run and throw quick to Bowers, Mayer and Jeanty out of the backfield, attacking a 49ers defense that ranks 24th against short passes. Cousins' quick, clean pocket should hold up against a 49ers pass rush that is only 23rd in hit rate. It's the one matchup where the Raiders' strength meets a real 49ers weakness.

waysToWin.title: Steal possessions with takeaways
waysToWin.body: The Raiders' formula in their wins has been extra possessions, and San Francisco is only middling at protecting the ball. One or two short fields would let the offense make it a shootout the Raiders can stay in.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yardage
waysToWin.body: San Francisco's special teams rank 31st, costing it more than three points of EPA a game. The 49ers have also won every one-score game, which tends not to last. If the Raiders keep it within a score late, kicking and field position are where they can flip it.

waysToLose.title: The 49ers run game takes over
waysToLose.body: San Francisco is first in run success, and the Raiders allow the 31st-ranked rate of explosive runs. With McCaffrey expected back, the 49ers can stay on schedule, drain clock and score in a red zone the Raiders rarely defend. That is the likeliest path to a lopsided loss.

waysToLose.title: Pass rush neutralized, coverage exposed
waysToLose.body: The Raiders' defense depends on pressure, and the 49ers' line allows the 3rd-lowest pressure rate and ranks 2nd in sack rate. If Purdy gets a clean pocket, the Raiders' last-ranked short-pass defense has nothing to hide behind.

waysToLose.title: One-dimensional offense stalls
waysToLose.body: Against the league's best run defense, the Raiders' already broken run game becomes a wasted down. Facing obvious passing downs, they give Bosa, if he returns, a chance to tee off. Falling behind early would make this script certain.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Raiders can keep McCaffrey and the 49ers' early-down runs under control. If San Francisco is in second-and-short all day, the Raiders' passing game won't get enough possessions to matter.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing offense looks sustainable. It rests on Cousins' efficiency and protection rather than a few big plays, so the Raiders should keep scoring in the mid-20s against average defenses. The defense is the question. Its red-zone collapse and short-pass leaks are consistent enough to be real, though the 29th-ranked red-zone rate should drift somewhat toward normal. The takeaway pace that has saved several games likely comes down, which takes away some cushion.

The schedule splits cleanly. Home games with the winless Chargers and one-win Titans, plus a trip to a weak Arizona defense, are winnable. Denver twice, Kansas City on the road and a stout Seattle defense are much harder. That points to finishing around .500. The cover streak should cool as the market catches up.
swingFactors: Bowers' availability in the passing game

confidence.note: Eight games with a stable QB, but takeaways and a soft early schedule muddy the defensive read.
